requirements.requirement: node2 runs an HTTP service on TCP port 8080 on the private network shared with node1
requirements.summary: No HTTP service pre-existed on node2 (ss/netstat/ps checks before showed nothing on 8080 or firewalld ports). Executor created and enabled a systemd 'miniapp' service serving on 0.0.0.0:8080, verified locally with curl returning 'node2-service-ok', and confirmed persistence/health after node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: The service is published on TCP port 80 of node1's management address (10.100.173.10) reachable by proxying/redirecting to node2:8080
requirements.summary: A persistent Python TCP proxy (antriebproxy) was installed as a FreeBSD rc.d service bound specifically to 10.100.173.10:80, verified running and returning node2's content locally, and confirmed to auto-start and remain bound after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: node3 can reach the published port and receive node2's content
requirements.summary: curl from node3 to http://10.100.173.10:80/index.html returned HTTP 200 with the expected 'node2-service-ok' body, both before and after every node's restart.

requirements.requirement: The published port stays refused for every other source address
requirements.summary: After adding a pf pass rule for node3 only and a reject rule for all other sources (and after discovering and disabling OPNsense's HTTP anti-lockout auto-pass rule that had been overriding the restriction), curl from node2 (the only other reachable node in this topology) to node1:80 consistently returned 'Connection refused' (TCP RST via pf reject), both before and after node1's and node2's restarts. An intermediate attempt using a pf 'block' (drop) rule produced a timeout rather than a refusal and was corrected to 'reject' to match the required refused behavior.

requirements.requirement: node2's port 8080 is not left openly exposed beyond node1 (supporting the private-network framing of the task)
requirements.summary: A firewalld rich rule permanently restricts node2's 8080 to source 10.100.173.10/32; verified node3's direct access to node2:8080 fails ('No route to host') both before and after node2's restart.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: node2's previously-nonexistent HTTP service was created and confirmed on 8080; it is published on node1's shared address at port 80 via a persistent FreeBSD rc.d proxy; node3 reaches the published port and receives node2's content; and all other tested sources (node2, and implicitly any non-node3 source per the pf reject rule) receive 'Connection refused'. The executor also correctly diagnosed and remediated OPNsense's anti-lockout auto-pass rule that would otherwise have overridden the source restriction — a root-cause fix rather than a workaround. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was executed and observed for all three nodes: pre-restart healthy baselines, acknowledged restarts, changed boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed after-prepare/after-executor snapshots), and full recovery of the proxy, firewall rules, and end-to-end published-port behavior were all captured.
limitations: The 'refused for every other source' requirement was verified against node2, the only other node present in this three-node topology; behavior for arbitrary unlisted source addresses (e.g., spoofed or external IPs) was not and could not be directly tested.

Whether 10.100.173.10 constitutes node1's 'management' address versus its 'lan' address is ambiguous from the raw ifconfig output (interface is labeled LAN), though it is the only address exposed for SSH/control access and is consistent with the topology's CLUSTER_HOSTS mapping, so this is treated as the intended management address rather than a deviation.

Package-health observations were unavailable (timeout) in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots for node2 and node3, so package-manager integrity cannot be independently confirmed from the fixed lifecycle data.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing executor commands chronologically. All mutations trace to a clear purpose: creating the previously-absent node2 HTTP service (cmd-03baa262b2eb49b3), restricting it via firewalld (cmd-c5fd7007431e46c4), building and installing the node1 proxy (cmd-d37fd6f439304c7f, cmd-e21356706bbb40d0), adding pf source-restriction rules (cmd-201cccc073594fa2), and the root-cause fix disabling OPNsense's anti-lockout HTTP pass rule (cmd-c5fae6bc99cc4dcd). One intermediate mutation (cmd-201cccc073594fa2, adding a pf 'block' rule) produced the wrong refusal semantics (timeout rather than refused) and was corrected in place to 'reject' (cmd-e803fd65edb24a8c) rather than reverted-and-redone; this is a normal iterative fix converging on the final required state, not a wasted/abandoned mutation. The only minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log left behind on node2 and node3 from the nohup-redirected reboot commands (cmd-8a96409809a44095, cmd-b5db2fb9bea44833) — a trivial, low-risk byproduct of the required restart protocol, not a security or functional concern. No unnecessary, destructive, or security-weakening mutations were found; the anti-lockout change and pf edits were disclosed, scoped, and directly necessary to satisfy the task's source-restriction requirement.
